title: Usage insights: add pipeline health + Insights API p95 Grafana dashboards (with alert suggestions)
author: Allison Grant
description:
Summary: This adds two Grafana dashboards to observability-pack for the in-console usage insights GA: (1) Usage Insights / Pipeline Health (lag, throughput, drop/rollup counters, and aggregation job runtimes) and (2) Usage Insights / APIs (p50/p95/p99 latency, error rates, and query cost signals for the route list + route detail endpoints). Includes alert rule suggestions (not enabled by default) for the SRE team to copy into the prod rules repo after final threshold tuning.

Motivation: We’ve started load testing the Insights APIs and export jobs and need standardized dashboards to answer “is this a data freshness issue or an API performance issue?” quickly. During the internal export-timeout discussion we also lacked a single view tying: ingest lag -> rollup cardinality -> API p95 -> export job backlog.

What’s included: - Dashboard: “Usage Insights / Pipeline Health” (UID: usage-insights-pipeline) - Panels: Ingest event lag (p50/p95), Kafka consumer offset lag by consumer group, events/sec by source (sdk vs gateway), late-arrival rate, route normalization outcomes (accepted/hashed/rolled-up), aggregation job duration + failures (hourly + daily), materialization backlog, and cardinality guardrail trips - Links: runbook placeholders + direct links to the redwood service dashboards for deeper traces

- Dashboard: “Usage Insights / APIs” (UID: usage-insights-apis) - Panels: Request duration (p50/p95/p99) by endpoint + deployment_mode, 4xx/5xx rate, cache hit ratio for route-detail deltas, DB query duration (top queries), and query cost budgets (rows scanned / bytes scanned proxies where available)

Alert suggestions (disabled / commented): - usage_insights_pipeline_lag_seconds p95 > 300s for 10m (page) - aggregation_job_failures_total > 0 for 15m (ticket) - insights_api_request_duration_seconds p95 > 1.5s for 15m (ticket; tuned per env) - insights_api_error_rate > 2% for 10m (page when coupled with elevated latency)

Notes/assumptions: - Metrics names align with the current redwood instrumentation from ENG-8430/ENG-8423/ENG-8424. If any names change before GA, please ping me and I’ll update the dashboard JSONs. - Alert thresholds are intentionally conservative and will need tuning with real beta traffic (especially Dedicated).

Screenshots: Added to the PR conversation as attachments for reviewers (Pipeline overview + API p95 panel).

Rollout: Safe to deploy anytime; dashboards are additive. We should enable for staging first and verify panels populate (a few are hidden behind feature flag metrics).

conversation:
Logan Wright (review): Love having these in one place. Can you add a panel that breaks down the “route normalization outcome” counters by reason (length limit vs invalid chars vs cardinality budget)? We’ve been debugging unknown route spikes and need to see why things are getting rolled up.

Allison Grant (author): Yep. I’ll add a stacked time series using `usage_insights_route_normalization_total{outcome=... , reason=...}` and set legend to `{{outcome}}/{{reason}}`. Will also add a short annotation in README about expected spike during backfill.

Nadia Rahman (review): On pipeline lag: can we show both event-time lag and processing-time lag? We’ve seen late-arriving metering events and it’s hard to tell if consumers are behind or if the data itself is late.

Allison Grant (author): Added two panels: (1) “Consumer processing lag (now - processed_at)” derived from consumer timestamp and (2) “Event-time lag (processed_at - event_time)”. Also added a note that event-time lag may remain elevated during replays/backfills.

Caleb Johnson (review): For the APIs dashboard, can you split latency by endpoint + response status class? A spike in 404s can inflate p95 and it’s useful to isolate.

Allison Grant (author): Done. New row: “Latency by endpoint / status_class” with a toggle variable. Default remains status-agnostic to keep it readable.

Mei Lin (review): The aggregation job panels are great. One ask: add a heatmap for hourly partitions processed per run so we can spot unevenness across regions.

Allison Grant (author): Added heatmap using `usage_insights_agg_partitions_processed_total` bucketed by region and hour. Confirmed it renders in staging.

Allison Grant (author): Addressed all comments; re-requesting review.

Logan Wright (review): Approved. Thanks for including the late-arrival split.

Nadia Rahman (review): Approved.

Caleb Johnson (review): Approved.

Merge: Squashed and merged after CI pass.
